content.title: About
content.content: Tuna salad with fat‑free dressing is a dish that combines cooked or canned tuna, fresh vegetables (tomatoes, cucumber, leafy greens) and a zero‑fat dressing such as yogurt‑based lemon vinaigrette. The combination provides a high amount of protein with low calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna is one of the richest natural sources of omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart and brain health.
Fat‑free dressings are often made with Greek yogurt, giving a creamy texture without added oil.
Tuna salads are a staple of Mediterranean cuisine and are popular as a light summer meal.
Canned tuna packed in its own juice retains most nutrients and has a long shelf life.
Fresh herbs like parsley or dill enhance flavor and add antioxidants.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Tuna provides about 25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: These polyunsaturated fats help lower triglycerides and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Thanks to the fat‑free dressing, the dish is low in calories, suitable for weight management.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna is rich in B12, niacin, and B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The salad supplies selenium, magnesium, and potassium, which aid immune function and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tuna.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Tuna can contain trace amounts of mercury; pregnant women and children should limit intake.

items.title: Sodium in canned tuna
items.content: Canned tuna often contains added salt, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Acidity of dressing
items.content: Lemon or vinegar in the dressing can irritate the stomach of people with gastritis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled; you can add boiled eggs, olives, or avocado for variety. It pairs well with whole‑grain bread or a flatbread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Store the dressing separately to keep vegetables crisp.
